subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or documented current-scope limits?
rationale: The report is credible and current code lacks the requested controls, but choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and security while an open candidate PR is already under review.

options.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with size/progress guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader backup-exclude tracker.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document the current backup limits and recommend plugin/workaround options only if maintainers decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement after resolving conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has the strongest recent current-main history on backup archive hardening and the current refactored files.
